sources.entry: marimo - A reactive notebook for Python, stored as pure Python and runnable as a script or app.

summary.one_liner: marimo is a reactive Python notebook that stores notebooks as pure Python files, runs as a script, and deploys as an app.
summary.what_it_does: When you run a cell or change a UI element, marimo automatically re-runs the dependent cells or marks them as stale, keeping code and outputs consistent. Notebooks are saved as .py files, and SQL cells can query dataframes, databases, CSVs, and Google Sheets, returning results as Python dataframes. UI elements such as sliders, dropdowns, and dataframe transformers bind directly to Python values without callbacks. Notebooks can be run as Python scripts with CLI arguments, served as web apps or slides, or run in the browser via WASM. The README also describes built-in package management, pytest support for notebooks, HTML export, Jupyter conversion via `marimo convert`, and an editor with AI assistance.
use_cases: replace Jupyter notebooks with reactive Python notebooks
build interactive data apps without Streamlit
query dataframes and databases with SQL from Python
share a data analysis as a web app or slides
version-control notebooks as plain Python files
convert Jupyter notebooks to marimo format
notable: Reactive execution: running a cell re-runs dependent cells automatically, or marks them stale in lazy mode
Notebooks stored as pure Python .py files, friendly to git diffs
Interactive UI elements bound to Python values without callbacks
Built-in SQL engine that returns results as Python dataframes
Can be run as a script, deployed as an app, or run in the browser via WASM
caveats: Some features such as SQL cells and AI completion require the optional 'marimo[recommended]' install
The README points to a free hosted service (molab) for cloud notebooks, but does not describe platform or paid-tier limits
